question: Can a single additional purchase on the original long winner's first closed 12H candle at or above twice entry improve realized monetary payoff and terminal wealth within 50% drawdown?
control: Reuse the 1585 funded native OKX V1.7 12H entries, no doubling sale, original two-thirds 2R first-12H limit and the fixed, minute-gap-checked doubling-candle low. Nine reserved seats and original directional exposures. No change to initial selection, exit triggers or leverage.
single_variable: At the next open after that first confirmation only, add to still-held child positions pro rata. At the specified stop (with both taker fees and the scenario market slippage), previous fills plus surviving units must leave enough locked profit to pay for the added quantity's entire loss. Size up to that profit budget, never exceeding available collateral after equal reservation for idle seats, 20% of NAV in current parent notional or 10% of the preceding 60 completed minutes' median USDT turnover. Skip if the regular hourly trim takes priority, the opening mark is at/below the floor, or input is missing. No retry.
fees: Original 5bp taker and 2bp maker per fill; additional stress of 5bp per market execution. Protection is conditional on the modeled stop fill. Price gaps, market impact, OKX funding, contract minimum lots and queueing are not fully represented. Report actual add participation relative to market trading when observed, separately from sizing.
evaluation: Compare relative to registered fixed-floor account, by original parent (not by addition), and by chronological period. Reconcile floor budget to true source-currency cash and open units, add sizing to all caps and terminal cash to parent sums. Baseline not rerun.
